The canonical record answers the reader question with audited annual and unaudited interim figures: FY2025 net revenues were 11,486 and Adjusted EBITDA 3,624, H1 2026 revenue rose 2.8% to 5,863 while Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.7% to 1,807, and in Q2 revenue grew 3.0% while Adjusted EBITDA fell 3.7% to 920 [C135, C128, C136, C137]. LTM Adjusted EBITDA to 30 June 2026 is 3592 and face debt 11807, so total leverage is 3.29x (calc: total leverage on face debt = 11807 / 3592 = 3.29x) [C127]. USD millions throughout; confidence is Restricted.

RBOT counts debt at face principal because the facility register is built from the debt note: 11,905 at 31 December 2025 and 11,807 at 30 June 2026. Balance-sheet carrying debt is lower, at 11,699 on the same date after discounts and deferred finance charges, so the two measures are not interchangeable [C125, C126, C127]. The GLPI and VICI financing obligations of 13,157 sit outside debt, and the filing estimates about 1.4 billion of 2026 lease payments to them, so debt-only leverage understates fixed claims [C138].

Reported EBITDA is operating income plus D&A, and Adjusted EBITDA adds back impairment, transaction costs and stock-based compensation. That bridge closes exactly in every column, for example 3,275 plus 349 of add-backs gives 3,624 for FY2025 [C128]. Segment history shows the mix shift: Las Vegas revenue fell to 4,049 in FY2025 while Regional held at 5,756 and Digital grew to 1,408; in Q2 2026 Regional rose to 1,570 and Las Vegas fell to 1,017 [C139, C140]. For creditors this is uneven cash generation, and one segment's strength should not be read as consolidated deleveraging without cash-flow confirmation.

Operating cash flow was 1,302 in FY2025 and 675 in H1 2026, against property and equipment purchases of 805 and 335 [C131, C141, C132, C142]. Cash interest paid for debt was 813 in FY2025 and 368 in H1 2026, with a further 1,349 and 686 of lease cash on the financing obligations [C129, C130]. Quarterly cash flows are not disclosed for Q2, so quarterly cash conversion is not established. Customer deposits and deferred revenue of 545 at 30 June are a funding float, not debt [C143].

What would change this view: sustained segment EBITDA, disclosed covenant headroom and debt reduction would strengthen it; lower H1 EBITDA, large lease commitments and the absence of any post-June reporting hold it back. The Alberta launch on 13 July 2026 is a subsequent event and is excluded from Q2 figures [C144]. Confidence in this module: Medium-Low.

CP-1A.analysis_md:
Four facts matter most to a creditor. Caesars is a large, lease-heavy and gaming-led operator whose Las Vegas segment is weakening while Regional grows partly through the Windsor consolidation; it has agreed to a US$31.00 cash take-private by Fertitta Gaming Holdco that is conditional and still pending, and the size of the new debt is not stated in the sources. [C78, C79, C52, C67, C80]

Operating model. FY2025 net revenue was US$11.486bn, led by casino at US$6.617bn, with hotel US$1.945bn, food and beverage US$1.714bn and other US$1.210bn. H1 2026 revenue rose to US$5.863bn from US$5.701bn while Adjusted EBITDA fell to US$1.807bn from US$1.839bn. For creditors, hold, visitation, labour, taxes and rent decide how much revenue reaches cash. [C81, C82, C83, C84, C85, C86]

Transaction and ownership. The signed agreement keeps Caesars as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent after the merger. The Carano family, with about 5%, rolls part of its stake. A US$200m company termination fee and a US$450m reverse fee apply in defined cases, and Parent's financing is not a closing condition. Funding terms, schedules and post-close capitalisation are not in the pack, so no closing probability is inferred and no pro forma leverage is inferred. [C52, C87, C88]

Governance view: Medium and incomplete. Reporting is audited and regular, and no repurchases were made in H1 2026, but acquisitions, a US$229m 2025 buyback and a small related-party lease are monitored items. [C63, C64, C89, C90]

Ratings: the pack shows issue ratings only, from FINRA (Moody's B1 and S&P BB- on the secured 2032s, Caa1 and B- on the unsecured 2032s). The corporate family rating B1 negative and S&P BB- on CreditWatch negative in the register are synthetic test values, marked as such, because no agency report was supplied. The downside path is a merger delay or weaker Las Vegas trading consuming cash while debt service and rent persist; the disclosed US$10m of merger costs is the first visible cost. [C80, C91]

Las Vegas earns 42.7% margin on 35.3% of revenue, Regional 31.1% on 50.1%, Caesars Digital 16.8% on 12.3%, Managed and Branded 24.0% on 2.4%.
The highest-margin segment is also the one now losing margin, so mix shifts EBITDA down faster than revenue.

CP-2.analysis_md:
Caesars is an adequate but cyclical credit: Credit Score 3 - Fair, Credit Direction Deteriorating, Sector Outlook Neutral, at Medium confidence. These three words are the module's illustrative view; the real CAOS run reached the overall view but not the labels. A large multi-property, multi-channel footprint and US$2,928m of liquidity support the profile, secured leverage is moderate (calc: senior secured leverage = 9468 / 3592 = 2.64x), and the weak point is cash flow after capex, cash interest and rent. [C16, C15]

Decision drivers. Support: 52 domestic properties in 18 states with casino, hospitality and digital operations give several sources of activity, though all share leisure-demand risk. Constraint: H1 revenue grew 2.8% to US$5,863m but Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.7% to US$1,807m, with Las Vegas weaker and Q2 Digital hurt by lower sports hold and higher gaming tax. Fixed claims: the FY2025 filing estimates about US$1.4bn of 2026 VICI and GLPI rent, and undrawn capacity is not cash flow or covenant headroom. [C14, C15, C20, C21, C13, C28, C22]

Financial profile. Carrying debt was US$11,699m (current portion plus long-term debt) against US$11,807m of face principal, with US$13,157m of lease financing obligations kept separate; cash was US$965m. Reported covenant compliance at 30 June is a positive fact, but no headroom is disclosed, so covenant capacity is not calculable. H1 operating cash flow was US$675m against US$680m, and operating cash flow less capex of US$340m is a proxy that excludes cash interest of US$368m, rent interest of US$686m and principal. [C23, C24, C25, C17, C26, C27]

The merger is the largest open variable. Parent has committed debt financing arranged by 10 banks and the deal is not subject to a financing condition, but the size and ranking of the new debt are unstated (G8); no closing probability or pro forma leverage is assumed. [C41, C42]

Counterweights and downside. Revenue growth, Regional and Digital earnings, liquidity and covenant compliance would strengthen the view if sustained alongside lower debt and disclosed headroom. The downside path is lower Las Vegas visitation or hold cutting EBITDA and cash while rent and debt service persist, raising revolver reliance and refinancing sensitivity; the nearest hard date is the 31 January 2028 revolver maturity. Further work needs post-June financials, the current credit agreement and covenant calculations, and the terms of the merger debt. [C13, C28, C16, C17, C43]
